headline: Computational design and scoring of biological sequences checked against experiment
label: Computational Sequence Structure Modeling
summary: Learned and rule-based models now generate sequences and variants that are tested against yeast import assays and rumen flux analysis.
synthesis: The dominant thread is computational generation or scoring of biological sequences and molecular variants, with outputs checked against physical or metabolic readouts. ProtGenesis maps amino acid assembly and mutation into trajectories in protein language model space and introduces spatial metrics to interpret them. TargetMITO generates synthetic mitochondrial targeting sequences from explicit rules and tests their import of nucleus-relocated OXPHOS proteins in yeast. The Ni(I)-inhibitor preprint links thermodynamic characterization and contrastive learning to rumen metabolic flux shifts, yielding an anti-methanogenicity score. X-Plat and AbiOmics are less directly aligned with sequence design, operating on expression and methylation data and transcriptomic marker genes. What distinguishes this group is the pairing of learned or rule-based models with experimental or systems-level validation.
